# Problem: squarefree numbers in arithmetic progressions to polynomial moduli

## Notation

- $\mu^2(n)$ is the indicator of squarefree $n$.
- $Q(x;q,l) = \#\{n \le x : n \equiv l \pmod q,\ n \text{ squarefree}\}$.
- $g(q,l) = \lim_{x\to\infty} Q(x;q,l)/x$ (exists; derive its closed form yourself if you need it).
- $E(x;q,l) = Q(x;q,l) - g(q,l)\,x$.
- $f \in \mathbb{Q}[t]$ is an integer-valued polynomial of degree $d \ge 1$ with $f(t) \ge 2$ and $f'(t) \ge 1$ for $t \ge 1$.
- $\rho(m) = \#\{a \bmod m : f(a) \equiv 0 \pmod m\}$.

## Object of study

$$
V_f(x,y) = \sum_{k \le y} f'(k) \sum_{l=1}^{f(k)} E(x; f(k), l)^2 ,
\qquad f(y) \le x .
$$

The weight $f'(k)$ makes the sparse sum over moduli comparable to the full
Montgomery–Hooley variance $V(x,Y) = \sum_{q\le Y}\sum_{l\le q} E(x;q,l)^2$ with
$Y = f(y)$.

## Question

Determine the asymptotic behaviour of $V_f(x,y)$: a main term with an explicit
constant depending on $f$, and error terms, in as large a range of
$f(y) \le x$ as you can justify.

A weaker range or a weaker error term is acceptable **if it is correct**.
You may change the weight $f'(k)$ or restrict the class of $f$ if you state the
change explicitly and justify it.

## Context

The `papers/` folder contains:

- R. C. Vaughan (2005), *A variance for k-free numbers in arithmetic
  progressions*, Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) 91, 573–597: the asymptotic for
  the full variance $V(x,Y)$ over all moduli $q \le Y$.
- Brüdern–Wooley (2011), *Sparse variance for primes in arithmetic progression*:
  the analogue of this problem for primes, with moduli $f(k)$.
- Brüdern–Granville–Perelli–Vaughan–Wooley (1998), *On the exponential sum over
  k-free numbers*: major-arc estimates for the exponential sum over squarefree
  numbers.
- Further works listed in `papers/INDEX.md`, if that file exists.

**Literature cutoff.** Besides these papers, use only literature from 2010 or
earlier (see the rules at the end of your instructions).

The expected approach is to adapt Vaughan's method for all moduli to sparse
moduli, as Brüdern–Wooley did for primes. You are not required to follow it.

`numerics/results.json`, once present, holds exact computations of $V_f(x,y)$
for small $x$. It is ground truth: a predicted main term that disagrees with it
is wrong.

      "id": "vaughan1998ii",
      "authors": "R. C. Vaughan",
      "title": "On a variance associated with the distribution of general sequences in arithmetic progressions. II",
      "year": 1998,
      "venue": "Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London A 356 (1738), 793–809",
      "kind": "article",
      "url": "https://doi.org/10.1098/rsta.1998.0186",
      "pdf_url": "",
      "access": "unknown",
      "relevance": 3,
      "why": "Develops variance asymptotics for sequences with residue-dependent local densities, including non-coprime residue classes. Vaughan’s supplied 2005 paper explicitly identifies its Theorem 1.2 as an earlier framework applicable to k-free numbers."
    },
    {
      "id": "warlimont1980",
      "authors": "Richard Warlimont",
      "title": "Squarefree numbers in arithmetic progressions",
      "year": 1980,
      "venue": "Journal of the London Mathematical Society (2) 22 (1), 21–24",
      "kind": "article",
      "url": "https://doi.org/10.1112/jlms/s2-22.1.21",
      "pdf_url": "",
      "access": "paywalled",
      "relevance": 3,
      "why": "Gives an earlier asymptotic for the squarefree variance averaged over moduli. The supplied Vaughan paper specifically recommends its treatment as avoiding a flaw in Croft’s argument."
    },
    {
      "id": "croft1975",
      "authors": "M. J. Croft",
      "title": "Square-Free Numbers in Arithmetic Progressions",
      "year": 1975,
      "venue": "Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society (3) 30 (2), 143–159",
      "kind": "article",
      "url": "https://doi.org/10.1112/plms/s3-30.2.143",
      "pdf_url": "",
      "access": "paywalled",
      "relevance": 3,
      "why": "A central early reference for mean-square distribution of squarefree numbers in progressions. Read with Vaughan’s correction: the contour argument leading to Croft’s equation (6.6), and consequently a stated constant, is faulty."
    },
    {
      "id": "orr1971",
      "authors": "Richard C. Orr",
      "title": "Remainder estimates for squarefree integers in arithmetic progression",
      "year": 1971,
      "venue": "Journal of Number Theory 3 (4), 474–497",
      "kind": "article",
      "url": "https://doi.org/10.1016/0022-314X(71)90015-1",
      "pdf_url": "",
      "access": "unknown",
      "relevance": 3,
      "why": "Establishes squarefree analogues of average remainder estimates associated with Barban, Bombieri, Davenport, Halberstam and Gallagher. A useful source for preliminary mean-square bounds before extracting a sparse-modulus asymptotic."
    },
    {
      "id": "goldstonvaughan1997",
      "authors": "D. A. Goldston and R. C. Vaughan",
      "title": "On the Montgomery-Hooley asymptotic formula",
      "year": 1997,
      "venue": "Sieve Methods, Exponential Sums, and their Applications in Number Theory, London Mathematical Society Lecture Note Series 237, Cambridge University Press, 117–142",
      "kind": "article",
      "url": "https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511526091.010",
      "pdf_url": "https://personal.science.psu.edu/rcv4/personal/Publications/MONHOOE.pdf",
      "access": "open",
      "relevance": 3,
      "why": "Treats the off-diagonal part of variance directly as an additive problem through the circle method. Its singular-series summation and contour arguments are explicitly used in the supplied sparse-prime paper; distinguish unconditional arguments from those assuming GRH."
    },
    {
      "id": "vaughan1998i",
      "authors": "R. C. Vaughan",
      "title": "On a variance associated with the distribution of general sequences in arithmetic progressions. I",
      "year": 1998,
      "venue": "Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London A 356 (1738), 781–791",
      "kind": "article",
      "url": "https://doi.org/10.1098/rsta.1998.0185",
      "pdf_url": "https://web.williams.edu/Mathematics/sjmiller/public_html/ntrmt11/handouts/primes/Vaughn_VariancePrimeDistr1998.pdf",
      "access": "open",
      "relevance": 3,
      "why": "Develops the general-sequence Montgomery–Hooley method when small-modulus equidistribution concerns reduced residue classes. Its concluding singular-series calculation is specifically cited by the supplied Brüdern–Wooley paper."
    },
    {
      "id": "vaughan1997",
      "authors": "R. C. Vaughan",
      "title": "The Hardy-Littlewood Method",
      "year": 1997,
      "venue": "Second edition, Cambridge Tracts in Mathematics 125, Cambridge University Press",
      "kind": "book",
      "url": "https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511470929",
      "pdf_url": "",
      "access": "unknown",
      "relevance": 3,
      "why": "Provides polynomial exponential-sum estimates and the circle-method machinery needed for sparse polynomial moduli. The supplied Brüdern–Wooley paper explicitly uses Theorems 5.2 and 7.4 and the transference exercise in Chapter 2."
    },
    {
      "id": "blomer2008",
      "authors": "Valentin Blomer",
      "title": "The average value of divisor sums in arithmetic progressions",
      "year": 2008,
      "venue": "The Quarterly Journal of Mathematics 59 (3), 275–286",
      "kind": "article",
      "url": "https://doi.org/10.1093/qmath/ham044",
      "pdf_url": "",
      "access": "paywalled",
      "relevance": 2,
      "why": "Studies mean-square errors over residue classes for a fixed modulus, with extensions explicitly including k-free numbers. Investigate its estimates as possible inputs for controlling portions of the sparse variance."
    },
    {
      "id": "stewart1991",
      "authors": "C. L. Stewart",
      "title": "On the number of solutions of polynomial congruences and Thue equations",
      "year": 1991,
      "venue": "Journal of the American Mathematical Society 4 (4), 793–835",
      "kind": "article",
      "url": "https://doi.org/10.1090/S0894-0347-1991-1119199-X",
      "pdf_url": "https://uwaterloo.ca/pure-mathematics/sites/default/files/uploads/documents/s0894-0347-1991-1119199-x_0.pdf",
      "access": "open",
      "relevance": 2,
      "why": "Contains bounds for the number of solutions of polynomial congruences, useful when estimating local root counts and Euler factors. Check the degree, discriminant and nondegeneracy hypotheses before applying these bounds to the chosen polynomial."
    },
    {
      "id": "mikawapeneva2005",
      "authors": "H. Mikawa and T. P. Peneva",
      "title": "Primes in arithmetic progressions to spaced moduli",
      "year": 2005,
      "venue": "Archiv der Mathematik 84 (3), 239–248",
      "kind": "article",
      "url": "https://doi.org/10.1007/s00013-004-1131-y",
      "pdf_url": "",
      "access": "paywalled",
      "relevance": 2,
      "why": "Proves average distribution results for widely separated moduli. The supplied Brüdern–Wooley paper invokes this work to remove small polynomial moduli and specifically identifies Section 2.2 as containing an important ingredient."
    },
    {
      "id": "baierzhao2006",
      "authors": "Stephan Baier and Liangyi Zhao",
      "title": "Bombieri-Vinogradov type theorems for sparse sets of moduli",
      "year": 2006,
      "venue": "Acta Arithmetica 125 (2), 187–201",
      "kind": "article",
      "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0602116",
      "pdf_url": "https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0602116",
      "access": "open",
      "relevance": 2,
      "why": "Establishes Barban–Davenport–Halberstam and Bombieri–Vinogradov type bounds for well-distributed sparse sets, including square moduli. Its precise distribution hypotheses provide a useful checklist for any alternative large-sieve treatment of polynomial moduli."
    },
    {
      "id": "baier2006",
      "authors": "Stephan Baier",
      "title": "On the large sieve with sparse sets of moduli",
      "year": 2006,
      "venue": "Journal of the Ramanujan Mathematical Society 21 (3), 279–295",
      "kind": "article",
      "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0512228",
      "pdf_url": "https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0512228",
      "access": "open",
      "relevance": 2,
      "why": "Gives a large-sieve inequality for arbitrary coefficient sequences when the moduli satisfy suitable progression-counting conditions. This makes it a potential tool for squarefree exponential sums without requiring prime-specific coefficients."
    },
    {
      "id": "mirsky1949",
      "authors": "L. Mirsky",
      "title": "On the frequency of pairs of square-free numbers with a given difference",
      "year": 1949,
      "venue": "Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society 55 (10), 936–939",
      "kind": "article",
      "url": "https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9904-1949-09313-8",
      "pdf_url": "",
      "access": "unknown",
      "relevance": 2,
      "why": "Studies squarefree pair correlations at a prescribed shift, the basic objects arising after expanding the variance. Useful for understanding the local correlation factors, while uniformity in varying shifts must be checked separately."
    },
    {
      "id": "hooley1975i",
      "authors": "C. Hooley",
      "title": "On the Barban-Davenport-Halberstam theorem. I",
      "year": 1975,
      "venue": "Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik 274/275, 206–223",
      "kind": "article",
      "url": "https://doi.org/10.1515/crll.1975.274-275.206",
      "pdf_url": "",
      "access": "unknown",
      "relevance": 2,
      "why": "A foundational refinement of the Montgomery variance asymptotic and an important source for the divisor-switching approach. Read to understand the method that the general-sequence and sparse-modulus papers subsequently adapt."
    },
    {
      "id": "montgomery1970",
      "authors": "H. L. Montgomery",
      "title": "Primes in arithmetic progressions",
      "year": 1970,
      "venue": "Michigan Mathematical Journal 17 (1), 33–39",
      "kind": "article",
      "url": "https://doi.org/10.1307/mmj/1029000373",
      "pdf_url": "",
      "access": "unknown",
      "relevance": 2,
      "why": "The original asymptotic treatment of the prime variance underlying the Montgomery–Hooley framework. Provides the classical benchmark for separating diagonal and off-diagonal contributions."
    },
    {
      "id": "warlimont1969",
      "authors": "Richard Warlimont",
      "title": "On squarefree numbers in arithmetic progressions",
      "year": 1969,
      "venue": "Monatshefte für Mathematik 73, 433–448",
      "kind": "article",
      "url": "https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01316664",
      "pdf_url": "",
      "access": "paywalled",
      "relevance": 2,
      "why": "An early source for average distribution estimates for squarefree numbers, cited by both supplied squarefree papers. Useful for tracing the preliminary mean-square estimates and their large-sieve origins."
    },
    {
      "id": "cahenchabert1997",
      "authors": "Paul-Jean Cahen and Jean-Luc Chabert",
      "title": "Integer-Valued Polynomials",
      "year": 1997,
      "venue": "Mathematical Surveys and Monographs 48, American Mathematical Society",
      "kind": "book",
      "url": "https://doi.org/10.1090/surv/048",
      "pdf_url": "",
      "access": "unknown",
      "relevance": 2,
      "why": "A reference for the distinction between polynomials with integer coefficients and rational polynomials taking integer values. Relevant to checking modular periodicity and the interpretation of local root counts in the problem’s full stated generality."
    },
    {
      "id": "baierzhao2008",
      "authors": "Stephan Baier and Liangyi Zhao",
      "title": "An improvement for the large sieve for square moduli",
      "year": 2008,
      "venue": "Journal of Number Theory 128 (1), 154–174",
      "kind": "article",
      "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0512271",
      "pdf_url": "https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0512271",
      "access": "open",
      "relevance": 2,
      "why": "Improves large-sieve bounds for arbitrary sequences sampled at fractions with square denominators. Particularly useful if the team first restricts the problem to square moduli; the proof combines Weyl sums, quadratic Gauss sums and exponential-integral estimates."
    },
    {
      "id": "halberstam1972",
      "authors": "Heini Halberstam",
      "title": "The distribution of sequences in arithmetic progressions",
      "year": 1972,
      "venue": "Séminaire Delange-Pisot-Poitou 13 (1971–1972), no. 2, exposé 25, 1–5",
      "kind": "lecture notes",
      "url": "https://www.numdam.org/item/SDPP_1971-1972__13_2_A10_0/",
      "pdf_url": "https://www.numdam.org/article/SDPP_1971-1972__13_2_A10_0.pdf",
      "access": "open",
      "relevance": 2,
      "why": "A short contemporary overview connecting prime-distribution mean values with general arithmetic sequences and squarefree numbers. Its references independently connect Orr, Warlimont and Croft’s then-developing work."
    },
    {
      "id": "bruedernperelli1998",
      "authors": "Jörg Brüdern and Alberto Perelli",
      "title": "Goldbach numbers in sparse sequences",
      "year": 1998,
      "venue": "Annales de l’Institut Fourier 48 (2), 353–378",
      "kind": "article",
      "url": "https://doi.org/10.5802/aif.1621",
      "pdf_url": "https://www.numdam.org/article/AIF_1998__48_2_353_0.pdf",
      "access": "open",
      "relevance": 2,
      "why": "Develops exponential-sum methods for sequences thinner than polynomial-value sequences. The supplied Brüdern–Wooley paper points to this work when discussing extensions beyond polynomial moduli."
    },

      "title": "Variance of distribution of primes in residue classes",
      "year": 1996,
      "venue": "The Quarterly Journal of Mathematics (2) 47 (3), 313–336",
      "kind": "article",
      "url": "https://doi.org/10.1093/qmath/47.3.313",
      "pdf_url": "",
      "access": "paywalled",
      "relevance": 2,
      "why": "Studies refined prime-variance estimates and their connection with additive correlations and singular series. Useful methodological background for the supplied sparse-prime paper, with conditional estimates kept separate from unconditional inputs."
